findings.issue_text: [BUG] The replacement NewInMemoryDB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go returns a stub whose QueryFramesInto, TablesList, and RunCommands all return errors.New("not implemented"), so every SQL expression execution now fails at runtime. Any dashboard using SQL expressions gets "not implemented" errors from expression evaluation; the diff removed the working github.com/scottlepp/go-duck implementation and shipped a non-functional stub in its place, silently breaking the feature rather than disabling it cleanly.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of the feature flag: it computes enabled as the negation of IsEnabledGlobally and returns false in both branches, so QueryTypeSQL requests are always rejected with "sqlExpressions is not implemented". Even when the FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle is enabled, the feature can never be used; the flag is a silent no-op and the gating logic is dead code.

[BUG] The diff removes the "github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck" import from sql_command.go but never adds an import for github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/expr/sql, which the new call sql.NewInMemoryDB() at line 96 requires, so the package does not compile. CI and all downstream builds fail with an undefined: sql compile error; the PR cannot be built as shown.

[ADVISORY] QueryFramesInto is declared with frames []*data.Frame but ignores all parameters and returns "not implemented", so the signature the caller relies on (name, query, source frames, destination frame) is a fabricated contract with no backing implementation. Callers in sql_command.go and TablesList in parser.go were written against go-duck's real behavior (JSON serialization output parsing in TablesList expects a successful RunCommands return); with the stub, TablesList's subsequent parsing of the ret string will never run and any error handling that assumed non-empty results breaks — the duckdb removal makes the entire sql expression subsystem a no-op shell.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions unconditionally returns false on both branches, so the feature toggle logic is dead and SQL expression queries are always rejected. Every user submitting a QueryTypeSQL expression query gets "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even when the featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions toggle is enabled, silently disabling the whole SQL expressions feature.

[BUG] NewInMemoryDB returns a stub whose QueryFramesInto always returns errors.New("not implemented"), replacing the working go-duck implementation. If the reader gate is ever fixed/flipped, SQLCommand.Execute (sql_command.go:100) fails at runtime with "not implemented" for every SQL expression query, and TablesList likewise always errors — the diff ships an inert feature with no functioning implementation and no tests covering any of it.

[BUG] The diff removes the go-duck import but never adds an import for the sql package whose NewInMemoryDB the code now calls. The package fails to compile (undefined: sql) unless an import was added in an unshown hunk; if sql refers to database/sql it is a type not a namespace for NewInMemoryDB and compilation still fails.

[ADVISORY] The entire DB abstraction is ships-inert: all three methods are "not implemented" stubs with no writer, no tests, and no callers other than the error paths. Operators enabling FlagSqlExpressions get a hard runtime error instead of analytics; the next change must reimplement or delete this file, and the go-duck removal strands the previous working behavior with no migration note.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of the feature flag state, permanently disabling the SQL expression query type. Both branches of the function return false (`if enabled { return false } return false`), so every QueryTypeSQL request hits the new error path in ReadQuery (line ~129) and returns "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even for users with the FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle explicitly enabled; the feature is a silent no-op that cannot be turned on without a code deploy.

[BUG] NewInMemoryDB replaces the removed github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck implementation with stubs that return errors.New("not implemented") for every method. If the feature-flag gate is ever fixed, SQLCommand.Execute (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-98) calls db.QueryFramesInto which unconditionally returns "not implemented", and TablesList (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23-25) calls RunCommands which also always fails — this diff removes a working SQL analytics implementation and ships non-functional placeholders, i.e. a ships-inert feature with no writer of real behavior.

[BUG] QueryFramesInto ignores the input `frames []*data.Frame` and mutates nothing, so even if the error were removed the caller's frame would never be populated. SQLCommand.Execute in pkg/expr/sql_command.go passes allFrames and expects the out-parameter frame to be filled; the stub signature accepts the frames but has no implementation path that writes to f, so any future un-gating of the flag produces empty results rather than query output.

[ADVISORY] The diff removes go-duck and its transitive hashes from go.mod/go.sum while simultaneously re-adding several of go-duck's transitive dependencies (JohnCGriffin/overflow, apache/thrift, klauspost/asmfmt, minio/asm2plan9s, minio/c2goasm) into go.work.sum. Maintainers running workspace builds get checksum churn for packages the main module no longer requires, obscuring whether go-duck removal is complete; the half-removed/half-retained dependency state means future `go mod tidy` runs will fight this file.

[ADVISORY] The flag-gating logic uses a double negative (`enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`) that reads as inverted intent before the unconditional-false bug even applies. The next developer who fixes this to actually enable SQL expressions has to mentally decode `enabled` meaning 'flag is disabled' then being negated again — a change-safety smell that directly caused the always-false bug landing unnoticed.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions always returns false: `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...); if enabled { return false }; return false` — both branches return false, so the FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle can never enable SQL expressions. Every QueryTypeSQL expression request returns 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' regardless of the feature flag state; even with the flag on, the SQL expression path is permanently dead, so operators flipping the flag see no effect and dashboards using SQL expressions always fail.

[BUG] The go-duck dependency is removed but its replacement DB is a stub whose every method (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) returns errors.New("not implemented") and discards all inputs (frames, query) — there is no working implementation anywhere in the diff. SQLCommand.Execute (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-98) calls db.QueryFramesInto which unconditionally errors, so any SQL expression that somehow passes the gate fails at runtime with 'not implemented'; TablesList also always fails. The PR ships a permanently broken feature behind a flag that itself never enables (see reader.go finding), meaning this code path is a dead stub with no test able to exercise real behavior — a stand-in shipped to production.

[ADVISORY] The disabled-path returns a generic error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' via fmt.Errorf instead of a typed errutil error, conflating 'feature flag off' with 'feature not implemented' in the message. Frontend users who send QueryTypeSQL get an unstructured error string with no error code to distinguish flag-disabled from truly-unimplemented, making support triage and UI handling of this state ambiguous; the flag-gate inversion above makes this the only message users ever see.

[ADVISORY] Execute constructs a new in-memory DB per query execution (sql.NewInMemoryDB() inside Execute) and passes allFrames plus an output frame into a method that the current stub ignores entirely — the dataflow contract (frames → query → frame) is carried by parameter convention with no interface or type enforcing that a future real implementation actually consumes the inputs. The unexported concrete *DB type (not an interface) means a future real DuckDB implementation cannot be swapped or mocked in tests without editing every call site, and the per-execution construction will multiply engine startup cost per query once a real implementation lands — the next change gets harder because call sites are bound to the stub struct.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions always returns false on both branches, so the QueryTypeSQL path now unconditionally rejects every SQL expression request with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'. The feature previously worked via go-duck; this diff silently removes that behavior and replaces it with a hard error for every user, with no human-accepted decision to disable the objective recorded — the accepted intent (SQL analytics support) was dropped during review iterations.

[BUG] The replacement DB stubs (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) all return errors.New("not implemented"), so the working go-duck implementation was swapped for non-functional stand-ins. Every SQL expression execution (SQLCommand.Execute via QueryFramesInto at pkg/expr/sql_command.go line 102) and every TablesList call (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go line 24) now fails at runtime; users who relied on SQL expressions get errors instead of results — the artifact no longer matches the original intent of a functioning analytics framework.

[ADVISORY] The flag-gating logic is inverted/dead: `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` assigns the negation and then both branches return false, so the featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions toggle has no effect whatsoever. Operators who enable FlagSqlExpressions expecting to restore SQL expression support get the same hard error; the intended escape hatch is a silent no-op, blocking any path back to the original objective without another code deploy.

[ADVISORY] Ships-inert interface: the new DB type exposes a three-method contract (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) but every method is a stub with no writer or real implementation anywhere in the diff, leaving callers in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go and pkg/expr/sql_command.go permanently broken. Any consumer of the SQL expression API (dashboard expressions hitting QueryTypeSQL) receives 500-class errors; the parallel hand-maintained contract between db.go's stubs and go-duck's removed real implementation has no path to convergence in this diff.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of the feature flag state, so the SQL expressions path can never be enabled and the feature gate is a silent no-op. When FlagSqlExpressions is enabled, the function computes enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(...) (inverted) and then unconditionally returns false on both branches, so every SQL expression query fails with "sqlExpressions is not implemented"; the security/control gate cannot ever allow the feature, and the dead boolean hides the inversion from future maintainers.

[ADVISORY] TablesList builds the DuckDB command via string interpolation of user-supplied rawSQL (fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)) with only single-quote doubling as escaping, a SQL string-interpolation pattern the diff preserves and re-points at the new DB stub. The moment RunCommands stops returning "not implemented" (the whole purpose of this framework), any user who can submit an SQL expression controls the full command text; quote-doubling inside a string literal is the only defense and any dialect that treats backslashes or nested quoting specially turns this into arbitrary SQL execution against the in-memory engine that holds all frame data. Authors' counter is that DuckDB string literals don't process backslashes and '' is correct escaping — that holds for vanilla literals, but the pattern invites breakage the moment the format string or dialect changes, and the raw query is attacker-controlled dashboard input.

[ADVISORY] The new DB surface (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) is stubbed to return errors, leaving the SQL expression execution path that parses and interpolates user SQL in place with no implementation of any result-size or statement-type restriction. When these stubs are filled in, the design has no allowlist (e.g. SELECT-only, single-statement) anywhere in this diff; whoever wires a real DuckDB in will inherit an execution path that runs arbitrary user-supplied SQL from dashboards with only the single-quote escaping in TablesList standing between the user and the engine — the security boundary is absent at design time, not just unimplemented.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions always returns false on both branches (the enabled=true branch returns false instead of true), so every QueryTypeSQL request is rejected with "sqlExpressions is not implemented". All saved SQL-type expressions and dashboards using them fail at read time with an error, regardless of the FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle state — a hard functional regression shipped in this diff.

[BUG] The replacement NewInMemoryDB is a stub whose TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto all return errors.New("not implemented"), replacing the previously functional scottlepp/go-duck implementation that this diff removes from go.mod. SQLCommand.Execute (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-102) now always sets rsp.Error for any SQL expression that gets past the reader, so every SQL expression query fails at execution time with "not implemented" — the feature is dead code end-to-end while its public API surface and the QueryTypeSQL contract remain.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions always returns false in both branches, so SQL expressions are unconditionally disabled regardless of the FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle state. Every QueryTypeSQL expression read returns 'sqlExpressions is not implemented', so users with the feature flag enabled still cannot use SQL expressions; the feature gate is dead code and the flag has no effect.

[BUG] The diff replaces the duck.NewInMemoryDB implementation with the stub sql.NewInMemoryDB whose QueryFramesInto always returns errors.New("not implemented"), breaking SQL command execution at runtime. Any code path reaching SQLCommand.Execute fails with 'not implemented' for every query; if the reader gate in reader.go is fixed or bypassed (e.g. other entry points constructing SQLCommand), execution silently degrades from working DuckDB queries to a hard failure.

[BUG] The diff removes the duck import but the diff shows no added import for the new sql package, so `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` refers to an unimported identifier and the package fails to compile. Build failure of pkg/expr; the package and everything depending on it cannot compile until the import is added.

[BUG] TablesList's RunCommands stub always errors, so parser.TablesList returns 'not implemented' for every SQL statement instead of a table list. Any caller of TablesList (e.g. variable/dependency resolution for SQL expressions) now fails on every input, and the reader-level gate does not cover these callers, so non-expression paths hitting this parser get a permanent hard error.

[ADVISORY] The new gate returns a bare fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") on a query-type dispatch path where other types return nil, surfacing an internal implementation status as a user-facing parse error. Users sending QueryTypeSQL expressions get a message describing an implementation state rather than a feature-flag-disabled error, making debugging misdirected; the message content misrepresents the actual condition (feature disabled vs. unimplemented).

```go

Authors' counter is that DuckDB string literals don't process backslashes and '' is correct escaping — that holds for vanilla literals, but the pattern invites breakage the moment the format string or dialect changes, and the raw query is attacker-controlled dashboard input.
